title: Fasting
english: The mouths of lions were closed, protecting those who were thrown into their dens. Fire, which had been raging in the furnace, miraculously fasted and did not consume the three men who were cast into it, thanks to the presence of a fourth, as described in Daniel 3:23-25. A sea creature fasted in the sea when it swallowed Jonah, as told in Jonah 1:17, and kept him safe in its belly. The sea creature had the prophet Jonah as a deposit and showed the sign of fasting by not digesting him.

Instead of being a threat, the sea creature carried Jonah safely through the sea, and eventually released him unharmed, returning the deposit to God. David fasted and repented, and through his fasting, God forgave him his sin with Uriah's wife, as seen in 2 Samuel 12:13. Elijah fasted for forty days and was given the power to control the rain, as stated in 1 Kings 17:1, and he could bring it or withhold it as he pleased. Our Savior fasted for forty days in the wilderness, as mentioned in Matthew 4:1-2, and in doing so, he shamed the devil and showed his sinlessness.

By fasting, Jesus gave us an example that through fasting, we can obtain forgiveness of sins. Let us fast, beloved, a pure fast, for as the apostle James says in James 1:27, pure religion is to visit brothers in their affliction and to keep oneself unspotted from the world. Jesus, the son of Nave, fasted and was able to command the sun and the moon to stand still. The apostles, who possessed nothing earthly, received authority from God to bind and loose, and this authority was fulfilled in them.
Peter and John, two of the apostles, went up to the temple at the ninth hour to pray, and they encountered a lame man who had been unable to walk since birth, and Peter responded to him.

title: The Gift of Health
english: Bodily health is more valuable than any amount of wealth, so I offer you health instead of the silver you were expecting to receive.
To be honest, I don't have any silver or gold to give you.
Christ has given us authority, and he instructed us, saying: 'Do not acquire gold or silver or copper' (Matthew 10:9).
He also gave us the authority to cast out demons, heal the sick, and cleanse lepers, reminding us that since we received our gifts freely, we should give freely as well (Matthew 10:8).
In the name of Jesus Christ, we are commanded to rise and walk.
While a servant may help someone up by taking their hand, the master heals with just a word.
It's clear that a servant is not greater than their master.
As medical facilities open around the world, I see Christ standing over all of them as the ultimate doctor.
What's remarkable is that different diseases, located in various hospital areas, are all treated by one doctor - Christ.
One person, struggling with the wound of sin, comes to Christ and, after receiving healing through fasting, departs.
Another person, having turned away from the stench of fornication, receives treatment for their spiritual foul smell from Christ, who heals both souls and bodies.
Then there's the person consumed by the fever of love for money, who, after being relieved through fasting, is able to find remedies for their disease.
Christ knows how to make sterile women conceive and turn a barren womb into a fertile field, giving prophets as a reward to those who fast.
The Bible tells us that Anna was in anguish, wept, and did not eat, but fasting gave the prophet Samuel to the barren woman.

Through fasting, Christ gives prophets as a reward to those who fast, and it has the power to dry up the sources of fornication, open the withered womb, and cut away the thorns of sin that sprout from our thoughts.

title: Spiritual Growth through Fasting
english: It no longer gives fruits of ungodliness. Fasting is beneficial not only for sinners, but also for the righteous, as we have shown. Through divine fasting, we can work on the stubborn, changing the unsympathetic into sympathetic people, and softening the hardness of the unyielding.

Moses fasted for forty days and forty nights and entered the darkness, and he saw God as no other human had. According to God's own testimony, if a prophet arises among the people, He will make Himself known to him in a vision, and speak to him in a dream (Numbers 12:6). However, with Moses, it was different, for God spoke to him mouth to mouth, face to face, as a man speaks to his friend (Numbers 12:8). Fasting has given the prophet a special gift of vision, transforming the face of the one who fasts into a more divine light, and it has given the prophet tablets written by the finger of God.

Let us approach fasting with a cheerful face, and let us greet it with joyful souls, abstaining not only from foods but also from sins. As we fast, we should pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord (Hebrews 12:14). We must not show ourselves humble in appearance to people, but be proud in our souls before the Lord, giving to the poor, and not stealing from others, and flattering God with words, rather than killing our brothers with our actions. Instead, let us fast from all evils, including foods, and say to Him: 'You have mercy on all, because You are able to do all things, and You overlook the sins of men for repentance; all glory is fitting to You, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and into the ages of ages.'
